source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Rounded woody shrub, usually ca. 1(–2.5) m tall
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Twice even-pinnately compound; 1–4(–5) pinna pairs per leaf [key]
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Very fragrant; petals separate; filaments distinctly pink, fading pale [key]
morphology_source_reported.fruits: 25–50 mm long; mature fruit 6–8 mm broad, typically few or no marginal prickles [key]

habitat_source_reported: Sandy or rocky open woodland and open ground
